rationale: C03 supplied the underlying regulatory text and organization for numerous provisions that the child expressly amends, including preparation for classification, the five classes and subclasses, Class I-C and I-D rules, and other classification machinery. The child repeatedly reproduces C03's provisions with targeted substitutions or additions, making C03 a concrete and material literal and structural drafting template. C23 and C17 are also strong antecedents for narrower clusters of the child's physical-examination and delinquency amendments, respectively.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 1622.2 of Part 1622 is amended to read as follows: § 1622.2 The five classes. Each registrant shall be classified in one of five main classes as follows...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 622.2 The five classes. Each registrant shall be classified in one of five main classes as follows...
shared_material.explanation: The child carries forward C03's complete five-class framework, renumbered into the later codification and amended in details.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 1622.3 of Part 1622 is amended to read as follows: § 1622.3 Subclasses. The five main classes are further divided into subclasses as follows...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 622.3 Subclasses. The five main classes are further divided into subclasses as follows...
shared_material.explanation: This is a direct reuse of the same heading, introductory sentence, ordering, and detailed classification list.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Paragraph (a) of § 1622.8 ... is amended to read as follows: (a) In Class I-D shall be placed any registrant who served honorably on active duty between September 16, 1940, and June 24, 1948, for a period of 90 days or more but less than 12 months...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 622.8 Class I-D... (a) In Class I-D shall be placed any registrant who served honorably on active duty between September 16, 1940, and June 24, 1948, for a period of 90 days or more but less than 12 months...
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces the distinctive eligibility rule and its two-part local-board determination almost verbatim while making limited substantive adjustments.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Paragraph (e) of § 1621.9 ... is amended to read as follows: (e) the local board shall not mail a Classification Questionnaire ... to a registrant who has not attained the age of nineteen years unless such registrant previously volunteers for induction.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: (e) The local board shall not mail a Classification Questionnaire (SSS Form No. 100) to a registrant who has not attained the age of nineteen years.
shared_material.explanation: The child directly amends C03's sentence by appending the volunteer exception central to the new directive.
